title: Police justified in fatal shooting, SIU concludes
article: Police in York Region were justified in shooting dead a 20-year-old man who took part in an early-morning home invasion three months ago and drove the getaway truck directly at the officers, the provincial body that investigates fatal police-civilian encounters has concluded.

"The police acted commendably in very difficult circumstances," the Special Investigations Unit said in a release describing the death of Shelton McKenzie, killed by a shotgun blast April 13 as he and another man tried to escape in a pickup belonging to the robbery victims.

Still a mystery, however, is how and why Mr. McKenzie and an accomplice came to be robbing not just the upscale Thornhill house where he died but also several other residences in and around Toronto over the previous six weeks.
Those who knew Mr. McKenzie -- a hard-working college graduate from a stable family who talked of becoming a policeman -- voiced shocked disbelief after the killing.
None more so than Mr. McKenzie's parents, who were "just blown away" by what happened, said the pastor at the Pentecostal church in Ajax that the family attends.
Violence was the hallmark of the five robberies linked to Mr. McKenzie and another man.
One target was Sherry Cooper, the chief economist at BMO Nesbitt Burns. On March 13, Ms. Cooper and her husband, Peter, were tied up at gunpoint as their home was ransacked.
"They were brutal," Ms. Cooper said of her assailants. "They clearly hated us [because of]what we had."

The fatal Thornhill shooting began with a 911 call after Mr. McKenzie and an accomplice allegedly broke into the Steele Valley Road home of Michael Thompson, president of Ontario Acoustic Sound Group, injuring him in the head.
When police arrived, two men were allegedly loading cash and assorted items into the family's pickup truck, which was parked in the garage.
The garage door opened and, with Mr. McKenzie at the wheel, the truck accelerated backward, the SIU said, narrowly missing an officer, who fired a shot but missed.

More police gunfire erupted as Mr. McKenzie put the truck into drive and tried to run down three more officers, the SIU said, but none of the seven bullets struck the two occupants. Only when another officer fired a shotgun did the truck come to a halt, rolling off the driveway and ending up in the road.
That blast to the side of Mr. McKenzie's head killed him. It also slightly wounded his companion, who fled on foot but was found shortly afterward hiding on the roof of a house a few blocks away.
Kevin Harris, 26, is in custody facing an array of charges stemming from a string of break-ins.
